2. What are aggregation and composition in Java?
Aggregation and composition are two forms of Has-A relationships.
represents a loosely bound Has-A relationship.
represents a tightly bound Has-A relationship.
The main difference is the dependency between the objects.
In aggregation, the dependent object can exist independently of the enclosing object.
In composition, the dependent object is strongly associated with the enclosing object and is accessed through it.

14. What are common real-world examples of aggregation and composition?
The following examples represent the relationships described:
The contained object can exist independently.
The contained object is strongly associated with the enclosing object.
For example, a chapter is considered part of its book, and an engine is treated as a component of its car in the examples.
The key distinction is whether the dependent object can exist independently of the enclosing object.
